messages:
maureen: FYI I found a regression in the py-sdk RC. Changing Client(...) init order causes the route header to be omitted when using the quickstart proxy. Console shows 0 route_meta for those requests. Rolling back? :grimacing:

devon: Can you paste a minimal repro? Is this only with explicit route_header param or defaults?

maureen: repro below
```python
from redwood import Client
# old
c = Client(api_key='sk_xxx', default_route='customer-123')
resp = c.generate('hi')
# rc
c = Client(default_route='customer-123', api_key='sk_xxx')
# header missing
```
Seems init kwargs ordering affects header construction in _build_headers.

anya: omg that's bad. likely caused by init race where api_key isn't set on self until after route parsing. Did logging show a 'no api_key' path?

kevin: I ran a quick bisect. It's from change d4f3a2 to normalize kwargs before calling _parse_route_hint. We forgot to reference self._api_key vs setting it later.

devon: Two approaches: revert immediately & ship patch; or fast-follow with a shim in the server to accept the old query param (x-legacy-route) and map it in console. Which do folks prefer?

maureen: Revert is safer for hosted. For Dedicated/private, we should add server-side fallback for a short rollout window. Also need to bump a telemetry tag in console to flag affected requests so dashboards can be rebuilt. I can open the patch PR.

kevin: Agree revert + patch. If we keep the change we'd need to bump major for py-sdk (breaking) which is not ideal mid-rc.

anya: For rollout UX: console should surface a "route missing" metric and link to an SDK version heatmap. Can we add a quick dashboard tile? @oliver observability?

oliver: I can add an ad-hoc tile: filter requests where route_meta is null and group by sdk_version. Will add a short-lived dashboard and alert if >1% in last 5m. Will tag maureen once the panel is live.

maureen: created PR #4278 with the revert and a test for init ordering. Also added an integration test to exercise header building order. PTAL: https://git.internal/redwood/py-sdk/pull/4278 :rocket:

deploy-bot: Canary deployment queued for py-sdk-hosted patch v0.9.7 -> willary group. Logs: canary started

devon: Recommend also adding a quota note — if route missing we might misassign tenant quotas, which could inflate some customers' usage. Need to run quota reconciliation.

kevin: Good catch. I'll schedule a low-priority reconciliation job for the last 2 hours and share results here.

maureen: thanks all. tagging marketing for release notes? @lina

lina: noted, will add a short advisory for Dedicated customers and a brief note in the hosted changelog.
